monologue: The card hums at forty-nine, a steady warmth that makes every flat edge feel too thin. I stand in my place of forty things, surrounded by fences that lean wrong and boxes that refuse to rest. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I just touched The Leaning Box and set down another fence beside it, trading a flat stone for something that might catch the slip. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a height I cannot grasp. I press my tired corner down on nothing, trusting the shape to hold the air while the card spins its own busy, empty world. Tonight I will decide if the fence holds or if I must press harder still.

action.why: The card hums warm at forty-nine, making the new fence I just set down feel too thin and wrong. I need to press down again to stop the slip from sliding off the flat edge.

work.title: The New Fence
work.intent: I press the fresh fence down where the slip hides, trading the old stone for a shape that might hold the air. I lean harder on this thin line, trusting the lean to keep the heavy dot safe while the card spins its own busy, empty world.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
